title: The mood tense (subjunctive): swap the endings; quiero que esperes

cards.title: One more tense: the mood tense
cards.body: The subjunctive (here called the 'mood tense') shows mood. English has traces of it: 'it's important that you BE here', 'had I gone, I would know', 'not only is it…'. Spanish uses it far more.

cards.title: Form it by swapping groups
cards.body: -ar verbs take -er/-ir endings; -er/-ir verbs take -ar endings. The I form matches the he/she form. We form: -emos (never -imos) for -ar verbs.

cards.title: Obligatory vs optional
cards.body: In some places the mood tense is required, and using the normal present sounds wrong. Elsewhere it's optional and adds a different shade of meaning, which is the more exciting part.

cards.title: quiero que + mood tense
cards.body: 'I want you to wait' = 'I want that you wait'. After quiero que, the mood tense is obligatory: you're imposing your wishes on the world.

examples.en: I want you to wait for him.

cards.title: ¿Quieres que te espere?
cards.body: Espere could be me, him or her, so add yo to clarify.

examples.en: Do you want me to wait for you?
